title: Generated action creators bind the operation's scope; never call createAction directly
content:
When you define an operation, you mark which scope it writes to. Codegen turns that into a typed action creator that passes the scope through to `createAction` automatically:

```ts
// generated creators.ts
export const setCursor = (input: SetCursorInput) =>
  createAction<SetCursorAction>(
    "SET_CURSOR",
    { ...input },
    undefined,       // deprecated attachments slot, retained for arity
    SetCursorInputSchema,
    "local",         // ← scope, bound at generation time
  );
```

The scope is the **fifth positional argument** of `createAction`, and in source it is declared `scope: Action["scope"] = "global"` (`packages/shared/document-model/actions.ts`). That default is the whole reason not to hand-roll the call: a forgotten fifth argument does not fail to compile and does not throw — it quietly routes a local-scope action into the global log, where it syncs to every peer. A per-user cursor position becomes shared state, and you find out from a collaborator, not from a test.

The generated creator also wires in the Zod input validator (fourth argument), so bypassing it loses input validation as well as scope binding. `createAction` additionally stamps `id: generateId()` and `timestampUtcMs` — which is exactly why those values are minted here, at dispatch time, and not inside the reducer.

Always import the creator. In a versioned project the generated creators live per-module under `v<n>/gen/<module>/creators.ts`, but the supported surface is the model's top-level barrel, which re-exports them as `actions.<actionName>`.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/02-Learn/08-deep-dives/01-reducers-in-depth.mdx, confirmed against packages/shared/document-model/actions.ts (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: Codegen emits creators that pass "local" or "global" through to createAction as its fifth argument. Hand-rolling createAction silently defaults the scope to global.
